page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at 2.7 GHz, delivering 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the CPU performance of this instance firmly in the average tier. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1452.0 and a multi-core score of 5294.0, with a PassMark CPU score of 11125.79. It supports advanced vector extensions including AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI, which assist in vector calculations and cryptography. However, memory performance is a notable bottleneck; while cached small-block reads reach 418.63 GB/sec, large-block uncached read and write bandwidths fall into the poor and weak categories at 21.36 GB/sec and 23.88 GB/sec respectively. This is reflected in a weak PassMark memory score of 1773.28 and lower-tier performance in memory-intensive Redis SET operations.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.c7.2xlarge offers a dedicated compute profile suitable for CPU-bound workloads that do not demand massive memory footprints or high-speed local storage. Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and the observed memory bandwidth limitations under large-block workloads, this instance is best suited for tasks like static web serving, software compilation, and light text or image processing. It is less optimal for large-scale in-memory databases or complex large-language model inference.
